business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global Employer of Record and Cross-Border Contractor Payroll

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state fiscal differentiation)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified civil-law administrative system with Anglo-American corporate law features introduced by Law 32 of 1927; territorial tax doctrine)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 31 October 2012)
Panama–European Union Trade Agreement (provisional application since 1 May 2013)
Panama–Spain Bilateral Investment Treaty and Double Taxation Convention (in force)
Panama–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (signed 2019; in force with effect from 1 January 2020)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 on Sociedades Anónimas (Panama Companies Law), Articles 1-58; complemented by the Código Judicial, Book II, and the General Regulations of the Registro Público de Panamá
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Departamento de Personas Jurídicas
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública / Pacto Social (Public Deed of Incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital; a minimum authorized capital of USD 10,000.00 is used to compute the public registry fee; no escrow account requirement under Panamanian law
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [PA_CORP] S.A. — At a duly convened meeting, the Board unanimously RESOLVED: (i) to ratify the subscription and issuance of capital shares by the founding shareholders, fully credited in the share registry; (ii) to adopt and maintain the registered office at [Panama City address], retaining the licensed resident agent (agente residente); (iii) to appoint the President, Secretary and Treasurer with customary powers; (iv) to open the corporate books, including the shareholders' registry and minutes book, and adopt the corporate seal; and (v) to authorize officers to execute municipal, tax and labour licensing filings. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Departamento de Nombres / Certificado de Búsqueda
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written name search application through a Panamanian lawyer (abogado idóneo) with three alternative proposed corporate names; upon clearance, obtain the Certificado de Búsqueda (30-day priority reservation) and include the approved name in the Pacto Social.
required_dossiers: Copy of the applicant shareholder's passport or national ID
Power of attorney granted to the Panamanian attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered entity, file an administrative petition citing alternative names or obtain a no-conflict letter from the prior registrant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública / Public Notary of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders execute the Pacto Social and corporate bylaws before a notary; the notary records the Escritura Pública and issues certified first-copy excerpts; all signatures are notarized and the deed is protocolized for registry submission.
required_dossiers: Draft Pacto Social and Bylaws prepared by the Panamanian attorney
Tax identification details of the founders, if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies errors or omissions, execute an amendment or reiteration before the same notary prior to registry submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Personas Jurídicas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deposit the protocolized Escritura Pública, first-copy excerpts, and payment proof with the Public Registry; after the legal compliance review, the corporation obtains its Folio Real inscription and the local representative is duly registered.
required_dossiers: Certified first-copy excerpts of the deed
Registry filing fee payment evidence (USD 250 minimum)
Legal review letter or annotation, if issued
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a preventive annotation (anotación preventiva) or rejects the deed, remedy with a corrective brief and supplementary act (acta aclaratoria), then reconsign the instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Share Subscription and Corporate Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal corporate governance / registered office records, witnessed by the licensed resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the constituent meeting; shareholders subscribe to shares and directors adopt Resolution No. 1 (per the pro-forma above); open the Libro de Acciones (share registry), Libro de Actas (minutes book) and dividend book; retain the original resolution in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: IDs of appointed directors and officers
Registered office lease or availability confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the minutes book is not yet available, record the resolution in a provisional notarized private act and re-register upon book opening; correct defects via a supplemental board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía/Municipio de Panamá — Dirección de Rentas Municipales
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación with the municipality, declaring the EOR activity (CIIU 7810 / NAICS 561330) and estimated revenues; pay the quarterly tasa única municipal fee and obtain the Licencia Municipal vigente.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried due to activity mismatch, file an amended aviso with the correct CIIU classification and pay the recalculated fee; administrative appeal is available to the Municipal Direction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) — Dirección de Empleo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the private employment agency operating authorization under Law 44 of 1995 (as amended), demonstrating operational capacity for global EOR payroll services, labour compliance policies, and designation of a labour-responsible legal representative; undergo an on-site verification if required.
required_dossiers: Corporate resolution designating the officer responsible for labour matters
Operational plan for payroll processing and contractor employment contracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of observations, address the ministry's requirement sheet (pliego de requerimientos) within the statutory term and resubmit; administrative recourse may be filed before MITRADEL's higher authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire Safety and Occupational Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (BCB) / Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral — Occupational Safety Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the office floor plan to BCB for a fire safety inspection and obtain the Certificado de Seguridad; present workplace risk insurance coverage (Riesgos Profesionales) and undergo occupational environment verification with MITRADEL for the physical office premises used for staffing operations.
required_dossiers: Office floor plan and evacuation routes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify flagged fire-hazard conditions (e.g., extinguishers, egress), request a reinspection, and if MITRADEL objects, present supplementary safety certifications and a corrective compliance plan.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) — Dirección de Empleo
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización de Agencia Privada de Empleo / Licencia Municipal de Aviso de Operación

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Sistema de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I — Exempt/Registration (office-only EOR operations; no full EIA report required)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharges; municipal wastewater connection must comply with ASEP (Autoridad Nacional de los Servicios Públicos) standards; zero VOC emissions from office activity; solid waste collection through licensed municipal haulers under Ley 41 de 2001.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (Certificado de Seguridad) issued by the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; municipal structural load adequacy confirmed under building-lease technical review for standard office occupancy; occupational workplace clearance under MITRADEL including Riesgos Profesionales insurance coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); electronic portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Panama Sociedad Anónima must first appoint a resident agent and register the corporation with the Public Registry. The company must then obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) from DGI, file an Aviso de Operación (business commencement notice), and register as employer with the Caja de Seguridad Social (CSS). For indirect tax purposes, the same RUC is used for ITBMS returns; application is made through authorized public accountants or via the DGI e-platform, requiring certified incorporation documents, resident agent appointment, bylaws, and identity documents of officers/shareholders.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Panama applies territoriality as the default statutory rule; companies may elect the Simplified Tax Regime for small taxpayers if annual gross income does not exceed the legal threshold, and may separately elect the Panama Fiscal Unit (PFU) settlement method for consolidation purposes. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available; transfer pricing documentation and advance pricing agreements apply for cross-border related-party transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — VAT-style consumption tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic turnover exemption threshold in B/.; any person habitually engaged in taxable transfers of goods or services, imports, or construction contracts must register for ITBMS. A simplified small-taxpayer regime is available to businesses with annual gross income up to B/.300,000, allowing reduced compliance obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama requires mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) for all VAT-registered taxpayers. Invoices must be issued through a DGI-authorized electronic invoicing system, transmitted in real time or near-real time to the tax authority via the Sistema de Facturación Electrónica (SFE) API, and validated with a secure digital fiscal stamp (código de impresión). Fiscal credit and export zero-rating claims require electronically accepted invoices and XML file retention.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of tangible goods qualifies for 0% ITBMS when the goods physically leave Panamanian customs territory and are evidenced by a valid customs export declaration. Services qualify for zero-rating only when the service is effectively used, exploited, or consumed outside Panama by a non-resident recipient, and the supplier maintains contracts, invoices, and documentary evidence of the offshore use and payment from abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera - DUA)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export
Commercial invoice issued under electronic fiscal invoicing rules
Inward Remittance Certificate proving payment from a non-resident client
Proof of actual offshore consumption for exported services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may conduct post-export audits to verify physical exit, offshore use, and actual foreign currency repatriation within 180 days. Failure to repatriate, false invoicing, or claimed zero-rating without substantive export documentation triggers reversal of the 0% rate, re-instatement of ITBMS at 7% plus late-payment interest, fines from 50% to 200% of the omitted tax, and publication as a tax defaulter. Criminal prosecution under Panama's Tax Penal Code applies for fraudulent export claims, including prison terms of 2 to 5 years and disqualification from doing business with the State.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — Panama has no central bank; U.S. dollar circulation and monetary policy are effectively managed via dollarization, with the SBP as the principal banking and foreign-exchange intermediary regulator.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy with the U.S. dollar as legal tender and the Panamanian balboa pegged nominally at 1:1. There are no exchange control laws; both current and capital account transactions are freely convertible. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, and capital repatriations are unrestricted and do not require prior central bank authorization. Non-resident investors may hold and transfer funds in USD without conversion hurdles. Corporate escrow accounts and operational accounts may be held in USD or other freely traded currencies, subject only to AML/KYC documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to repatriate or convert export proceeds. Earnings from global EOR staffing and payroll services may be retained in USD abroad or transferred into Panama freely and immediately. There is no foreign-exchange surrender requirement for receipts invoiced in USD or any other currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Payroll Disbursement Account
Operational Treasury Account with Multi-Currency Capabilities
Capital Escrow Account and Corporate Operational Account
Operational Account for Local Payroll Clearing
Cross-Border Treasury and Private Client Settlements Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with legal restrictions. Panama does not have a dedicated 'electronic money institution' (EMI) statute comparable to the EU EMI directive. A foreign digital EMI (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business) may only operate through an approved Panamanian banking partner or a locally licensed finance company, and must obtain a brokerage or money-transmission license from the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá if it establishes a physical presence or targets Panamanian residents. For a pure offshore payouts engine, a regulated foreign EMI may be used for cross-border contractor disbursements without a Panama license, provided the funds never trigger regulated money-services activity inside Panama. This approach carries legal uncertainty; a tier-1 Panama correspondent bank remains the preferred compliant clearing channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one director, final beneficial owner, or authorized signatory is generally mandatory for a standard corporate account opening at Panamanian banks. Remote opening is permitted in limited cases where the corporate client has an existing relationship, the bank's risk committee approves, and all KYC documents are notarized, apostilled, and verified via a correspondent bank in the client's home jurisdiction. For the Sociedad Anónima used as a global EOR platform, the statutory agent (resident agent) must physically attend or arrange a qualified notarized representation; the ultimate beneficial owner may complete a video interview with digital identity verification if the bank's policy allows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained high-frequency cross-border payment volume inconsistent with the stated staffing services model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Service agreements with client enterprises; audited sample of client invoices and payroll run reports; employer-of-record contracts for each underlying worker; detailed beneficiary records matching payroll ledger entries; tax and social security filing evidence in jurisdictions where payroll services are delivered.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the corporate purpose code (staffing services) and actual remittance beneficiaries being individuals in diverse jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Power-of-attorney and vendor payment authorization matrix; global employment contracts or independent contractor agreements; cumulative payroll register; regulatory licenses of the EOR platform; reconciliation of SWIFT purposes codes (e.g., 'Management Fees' or 'Staff Hire' for outbound) with a formal economic substance file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Panama S.A. has no physical office outside its registered agent while conducting multi-country payroll operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for a Panama administrative office; employment contracts of local staff (finance director, compliance officer, AML officer); registered agent certificate; financial statements reflecting operational substance; undertaking to maintain records under Panama's corporate law and AML regulations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound investor capital injection routed from a jurisdiction perceived as high-risk without clear source-of-funds documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of the parent entity or investor; notarized board resolution authorizing the injection; executed subscription agreement or intercompany loan agreement with commercial terms; declaration of source of wealth; certificate of good standing of the investing entity; supporting documents for Benford law-compliant transaction granularity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a payments aggregator (e.g., Wise) for outbound payroll creating a perceived opacity around ultimate recipients
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Aggregator monthly settlement reports; sub-ledger of each contractor with name, country, amount, and tax identifier; signed KYC files on each contractor; AML risk assessments performed before the first payout; a compliance manual demonstrating transaction monitoring and sanctions screening.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital may be wired via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's corporate bank account directly to the Panama S.A. corporate operational account. No Panamanian exchange-control approval is required because Panama is dollarized. Recommended purpose code for the wire is 'Capital Contribution' (services sector code) or 'Equity Injection' under ISO 20022 equivalent codes. The bank may require a board resolution, a certified copy of the share register, and source-of-funds statements. To maintain clean clearing, route injections from a regulated bank in the investor's home country, avoid third-party intermediary accounts, and refrain from cash couriered deposits. For multi-currency injections in EUR or GBP, the receiving Panama bank will automatically convert to USD at prevailing market rate; maintain a documented prior approach with the treasury desk to obtain transparent pricing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for global EOR payroll and staffing settlements should be executed via SWIFT MT103 corporate-to-beneficiary payments for supplier invoices and contractor payroll, with purpose codes such as 'Business Services' or 'Staff Hire'. For high-value outbound remittances exceeding USD 50,000, implement dual-authorization under a positive-pay system. For payments to jurisdictions with exchange restrictions, commercial letters of credit (LCs) may be used only for physical goods or where the EOR client requires trade-finance instruments; for pure service settlements, the standard clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 with settlement through the correspondent bank (e.g., JPMorgan, Citi, BNY Mellon, or Bank of America). Include the S.A. treasury invoice reference in field 70 (remittance information) to ensure audit trails. Do not use cash sweeps or unhosted wallets. Where local payroll must be paid in local currency (e.g., Costa Rican colón, Colombian peso), utilize the Panama bank's multi-currency platform or a licensed payment provider with clear sub-ledger and full audit ability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla currency forwards (USD/EUR, USD/GBP, USD/MXN) for known future payroll obligations
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) against restricted LATAM currencies to hedge payroll exposures where physical delivery is not permissible
Cross-currency interest rate swaps only when linked to an underlying real borrowing or receivable and approved by the bank's market-risk committee
FX spot transactions for operational conversion needs
Currency swaps executed with a regulated Panamanian or Tier-1 international bank for mitigating long-duration contract liability
Options on major currency pairs for uncertain staffing demand, subject to board-approved treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 31 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest, surcharge of 10%, statutory fines, ineligibility for certificates of good standing, and administrative strike-off risk if left unpaid for successive years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Anual de Rentas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 immediately following the December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of the tax due, monthly interest, fines, suspension of the taxpayer identification number (RUC), and administrative enforcement/property embargo in case of persistent delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) under Law 70 of 2019 and its implementing rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual review aligned with the income tax return; shareholder transfer updates filed within 15-30 calendar days after the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalty per unsworn/inexact filing, per-day fines for delayed updates, and for repeat violations, risk of registry intervention and administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory external tax audit by a Panamanian certified public accountant (CPA) when annual gross income or total assets exceed USD 3,000,000; lower threshold may apply for companies operating under licensed/supervised EOR and payroll activities, or when lending institutions require audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for entities required to produce audited and published financial statements; local tax basis accounting (Panama General Accounting Principles) accepted for small and medium taxpayers when audited statements are not required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Ultimate beneficial owners must be identified at registration and whenever share transfers occur; for each transfer the register of members is updated, the resident agent captures new beneficial ownership data, and a confidential annual confirmation is filed with DGI identifying natural persons holding 10% or more of shares or otherwise exercising effective control.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Officers (Registro de Directores y Funcionarios)
Share Transfer Ledger (Registro de Transferencia de Acciones)
Resident Agent and Registered Office Records

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat rate on net taxable Panama-source income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday applies to EOR/staffing activities. Effective mitigation arises from (i) strict territorial scope excluding foreign-source EOR fees from the taxable base, and (ii) tax loss carryforward rules. Additional reductions apply only in special regimes (multinational headquarters SEM, Ciudad del Saber) which require separate licensing and substantive commitments.
